newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian cargo spacecraft to burn up on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Russian cargo spacecraft to burn up on Wednesday.

text.p: An unmanned Russian space craft will burn up on Wednesday but some parts will crash into the Pacific Ocean, a mission control spokesman said on Tuesday.
The Russian space authorities decided to let the Progress M-33 cargo vessel burn up after it failed to dock with the Mir orbiting station.
"The Progress M-33 space craft will enter the upper part of the Earth's atmosphere and burn up there at 6:23 a.m. Moscow time (0423 GMT)," the spokesman said.
"About 200 kg of metal will fall into the Pacific Ocean at a distance of 3,150 km (1,970 miles) east of Wellington, New Zealand."
None of the parts that fall into the sea would be radioactive, he said.
The Progress M-33 has been in orbit since November 1996 and delivered water, food, air and fuel to the Mir crew.
It de-docked from Mir on February 6 to make way for a Soyuz TM-25 craft which brought up a replacement crew to the orbiting station, but efforts to link it back to Mir failed.
Russian engineers had been trying to dock the Progress with Mir to check a new docking system, but were unsuccessful.
Vladimir Solovyov, the head of Russia's space flights programme, said last week the Progress contained only rubbish from Mir and that it had enough fuel to help it out of orbit.
